comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose matching contributions for US-defined contribution plans with specific expense amounts for 2024. Intel expensed $541 million in 2024 for matching contributions, having increased the matching rate in 2024 compared to prior years. AMD’s 401(k) plan matches 75% of employee contributions up to 6% of eligible compensation, resulting in approximately $78 million in contributions for 2024. While both companies offer similar 401(k) matching structures for US employees, Intel's 2024 matching expense ($541 million) was significantly higher than AMD's ($78 million), and Intel explicitly noted an increase in the matching rate for 2024, whereas AMD's contribution amount increased from $70 million in 2023 to $78 million in 2024 without an explicit mention of a structural rate change in the provided text.

sentences.text: We expensed $541 million in 2024, $272 million in 2023, and $489 million in 2022 for matching contributions based on the amount of employee contributions under the US qualified defined contribution and non-qualified deferred compensation plans.
The matching contribution in the US qualified defined contribution plan was increased from January 1 through December 31, 2024 as compared to 2023 and 2022.
The Company matches 75% of employees' contributions up to 6% of their eligible compensation.
The Company's contributions to the 401(k) plan for 2024, 2023 and 2022 were approximately $78 million, $70 million and $47 million, respectively.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company matches U.S. employee 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to 6% of eligible earnings, with immediate vesting, resulting in $210 million in contributions for fiscal year 2024, an increase driven by the VMware Merger.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom (AVGO) disclose U.S. 401(k) matching contributions and expenses for fiscal year 2024. Intel expensed $541 million for matching contributions and increased its matching rate in 2024 compared to 2023. Broadcom matched employee contributions dollar-for-dollar up to 6% of eligible earnings, contributing $210 million in fiscal 2024, an increase from $100 million in 2023 attributed to the VMware Merger. Both companies show an increase in matching contribution expenses for 2024 compared to the prior year, though Intel's expense was substantially larger ($541 million vs $210 million) and Intel cited an increase in the matching rate, while Broadcom cited acquisition-driven headcount increases.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company maintains a 401(k) plan for U.S. employees matching cash contributions up to 5% of eligible earnings, with an expense of $66 million in 2024. Employees may contribute up to 75% of eligible pay, subject to IRS limits, without direct investment in company stock.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron (MU) disclose matching contributions for US retirement plans with specific 2024 expense figures. Intel expensed $541 million in 2024 for matching contributions, having increased the matching rate in 2024. Micron matched eligible contributions up to 5% of eligible earnings, with a 401(k) contribution expense of $66 million in 2024, up from $59 million in 2023. Both companies report an increase in matching contribution expenses for 2024 compared to 2023, but Intel's expense magnitude ($541 million) is much higher than Micron's ($66 million), and Intel explicitly details a change in the matching rate structure for 2024, whereas Micron only discloses the expense amount and match percentage without specifying a rate change.
